I do try to tell myself it could just be coincidence, and maybe I’m reading too much into it, but I can’t really shake it. I thought it might be worth talking to someone before I let it affect me more.\n\nDoctor: Right now, do you believe for certain that these people are tracking your client meetings?\n\nPatient: I wouldn’t say I can prove it, and I know that probably sounds… not great. But yes, a pretty strong part of me believes it’s happening. I keep trying to talk myself into it being coincidence—like invitations or panel topics or who ends up near me at events—but I can’t really let it go. I don’t want to come in here acting like I have absolute proof or anything. I know there’s a chance I’m connecting things that aren’t actually connected.\n\nBut at the same time, it’s been hard for me to dismiss it. The invitations, the topics at panels, who ends up sitting near me at events… it starts to feel like little signals about which clients I’m meeting with. So I can say I might be mistaken, but I guess I don’t fully feel mistaken, if that makes sense.\n\nDoctor: Even when other people tell you there’s probably an ordinary explanation, are you still convinced these signals are definitely about your client meetings?\n\nPatient: I… I wouldn’t want to say “definitely” like I’m trying to be unreasonable. I do hear people when they say there could be an ordinary explanation, and part of me wants that to be true.\n\nBut honestly, yes, I still feel pretty convinced that the invitations and panel topics and even who ends up sitting near me are connected to which clients I’ve been meeting with. I know that may sound like I’m reading into things, but it’s hard for me to shake.\n\nDoctor: If someone you trust offered a convincing ordinary explanation for these events, do you think you could accept that you might be wrong?\n\nPatient: I think… yes, I’d like to say I could.
